question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Twin-population lineage barcoding to retrospectively profile future survivors: Introduce expressed heritable barcodes into the cell line, split the population into treated and untreated halves, and identify the barcodes enriched after drug treatment. Then profile the matched untreated sibling cells carrying those same barcodes to directly measure the pre-existing molecular state that predicted survival, rather than inferring it from survivors already altered by the drug.
2. Live-cell imaging of signaling and cell-cycle dynamics across the treatment window: Use fluorescent reporters for target-pathway activity, cell-cycle phase, apoptotic commitment, and stress responses, and track individual cells continuously from before dosing through survival or death. This yields each survivor's full dynamic history, distinguishing cells that never engaged the drug target from those that engaged it but failed to commit to death.
3. Single-cell transcriptomic time course of persistence and regrowth: Profile the population at closely spaced timepoints spanning naive, early drug exposure, deep persistence, and regrowth, and compare the trajectories. This tests whether survivors enter one convergent tolerant program or several distinct ones, and whether the surviving state reverts to the naive distribution after drug withdrawal.
4. Chromatin accessibility mapping plus epigenetic modifier perturbation: Perform single-cell ATAC-seq on naive, persister, and regrown cells to find regulatory regions that are already open in the rare subpopulation before treatment. Then test causality by knocking down or inhibiting the chromatin modifiers maintaining those regions and asking whether the frequency of survivors drops.
5. Schedule and dose manipulation to separate reversible tolerance from fixed resistance: Systematically vary dose, treatment duration, and drug-holiday length, then re-challenge the expanded survivors and quantify how often they survive again. If survival frequency resets toward the parental rate after a holiday, the state is reversible and non-genetic; if it is retained, genetic or stably heritable mechanisms dominate, which can be confirmed by sequencing resistant clones.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Single-cell drug exposure and target occupancy as the null model
ideas.description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging), efflux activity, and actual target engagement (NanoBRET or in-cell occupancy reporter), then ask whether survivors occupy the low-occupancy tail. This tests the rarely measured possibility that fractional survival reflects pharmacological heterogeneity in uptake, efflux, and target abundance rather than any distinct regulatory cell state.

ideas.title: Sister-pair concordance decay to measure the memory half-life of the survival state
ideas.description: Reconstruct lineage trees by imaging up to the moment of dosing and score survival concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives as a function of generations since their common ancestor, yielding a model-free estimate of how long the predisposing state is inherited. Combine with quantification of what is asymmetrically partitioned at those divisions (mitochondria, lysosomes, efflux pumps, protein aggregates) to nominate the physical carrier of that memory.

ideas.title: Fluctuation-test design to extract state-switching rates instead of state identities
ideas.description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style experiments with many parallel small cultures expanded for different numbers of generations before treatment, and fit the variance structure of survivor counts to estimate forward and backward switching rates between tolerant and sensitive states. Using only colony counts, this distinguishes rare stochastic switching, continuously fluctuating traits, and pre-existing stable subclones, and produces rate constants that any mechanistic model must reproduce.

ideas.title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as a prospective functional predictor
ideas.description: Apply BH3 profiling (single-cell or on sorted fractions) to the naive population to map how close each cell sits to the mitochondrial death threshold, and prospectively sort on mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial mass, or sensitizer-peptide response before any drug exposure to test enrichment for survivors. This asks whether survival is set by the death machinery's setpoint rather than by target-pathway signaling or transcriptional identity.

ideas.title: Survival as a neighborhood property rather than a cell-intrinsic property
ideas.description: Image the local context of every cell at the moment of dosing (local density, contact number, neighbor identity, distance to colony edge) and regress survival on these variables, then manipulate context directly with micropatterned colonies of defined size, density-matched seeding, and conditioned-medium or transwell swaps. If local secreted factors or contact confer survival, cell-autonomous profiling approaches will only ever recover correlates of position rather than causes.
